findings.title: Deposit is within the amount cap
findings.detail: This amount check does not verify deposit protection or authenticity. Annual rent GBP 15600; cap = 15600 / 52 * 5 (GBP 1500.00 rounded down to pennies); requested GBP 1500. Importance: 85/100. Conditional: Confirm that the rented property is in England. Confirm this is an ordinary private tenancy, not an excluded arrangement. Confirm that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The cap arithmetic holds on the quoted figures. Rent is GBP 1300 per calendar month (s5), so annual rent is GBP 15,600. Five weeks is GBP 1500.00, and the deposit of GBP 1500 (s6) is at the cap, not above it. This is a correctly limited amount-cap pass, and nothing in the contract contradicts the figures. It remains conditional because the context leaves jurisdiction and tenancy type unknown. The contract does not state that the property is in England, and nothing confirms this is an ordinary covered private tenancy or that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The cap result says nothing about deposit protection or authenticity. s11 leaves the scheme details to be provided separately, and that is a different matter from this amount check. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tenant-fees-act-2019-guidance-for-tenants
